title: GPS & Load Dashboard
tagline: Full-stack GPS, wellness and strength platform for youth academy categories
problem: A football club's youth-academy performance department needed to turn raw GPS exports, wellness forms and strength tests into usable daily information — with zero cloud cost and without processing sensitive athlete data outside club machines.
targetUser: Coaching and physiology staff of the youth academy (U15/U17/U20).
myRole: Sole developer: architecture, data pipeline, backend, frontend, deploy.
process: Started in Streamlit to validate the workflow with staff, then migrated to a monorepo: Next.js + React + Tailwind webapp, local FastAPI + pandas backend, SQLite as source of truth, Tauri desktop shell. Incremental Google Drive sync (by modified time) for GPS, wellness and strength files; optional one-way local → cloud sync (always upsert) for remote reads.
keyDecisions: Local-first: no raw file ever processed in the cloud; zero hosting cost.
No business calculations in the database or frontend — a single Python layer.
Natural-key upserts everywhere; never plain inserts.
Athlete-name resolution via fuzzy matching against a central registry, with a manually reviewed pending queue (unresolved names never enter the DB).
Strength data local-only in v1 — smaller exposure surface.
result: Production platform with 11 modules: daily GPS session, week-over-week reports with targets, load/RPE, live monitoring, individual athlete profile, wellness (Hooper + post-training + assessment calendar), strength (3 devices), athlete/loan management, sync admin, and client-side PDF export. Thousands of records processed per season.
learned: The name coming from the source ecosystem beats the official registered name for matching — "pretty name" matching produces false positives on common surnames. And keeping all computation in one layer pays off fast: swapping the visualization layer (Streamlit → Next.js) didn't touch the pipeline.
